findings.reason: as written the node must either report a control that cannot fire or seed and drive a review record the fixture does not have, and the confinedness claim the control exists to establish would go unproven; dropping `checked_at` via `_VOLATILE_KEYS` would then pass every declared control, since the parity case compares no view that carries one.
findings.text: the done-when's second control ("keeps the drop but compares a review view's stored `checked_at` altered on one surface, and the case still fails, showing the drop is confined to the budget view") names a `checked_at` that no view the parity case drives carries: the only such field the section cites sits inside `compose_review` (reckon/mcp_views.py:1367), whose output is reached through the plan/roadmap document path (`reckon/serve.py:1693`, `reckon/roadmap.py:3665` via `load_composed_review`), not through any of the nineteen crew views the case iterates (`CREW_VIEWS`, reckon/mcp_views.py:3598–3619), and the test's own fixture plants no stored review record (`tests/test_crew_view_serves_every_view.py:134` writes a ledger *run* row `r-review`; no review singleton is written into the synthesised project) — so on the fixture the case runs against, there is no nested `checked_at` for the control to alter, and the control cannot fire

rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold. The stated root cause matches its cited evidence (I re-derived it from the cited capture: the two budget documents differing by one 30-second clock step differ in exactly one leaf, `/checked_at`; `captured.json` call 1 vs call 2, 1 differing leaf of 118). The mechanism produces the done-when: patching `budget._now` changes the value `preflight` stamps into the view's top-level `checked_at` (reckon/budget.py:2114 `moment = _now(now)`, emitted at :2227), and the drop removes the leaf the clock moves. It runs on the real code path with the caller named: `serve_crew_view` composes the budget view through `budget_module.preflight(...)` (reckon/mcp_views.py:3922), and both surfaces reach it in-process — `_served_by_the_tool` calls `mcp._crew(...)` and `_served_by_the_cli` uses `CliRunner().invoke(main, ...)`, so a `monkeypatch.setattr(budget, "_now", ...)` reaches both, which the previous review's probe run confirmed by capturing both surfaces' documents with the counter advancing once per call.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, that the parity case reads the budget view at one instant; the three clocks/controls are measures of it, not a second deliverable.
